title: Design: KDF UAPI struct and provider callback contract
description:
Define the ioctl struct and provider API before any implementation.

UAPI struct (crypto2dev_kdf_op):
  algo[64]:          'hkdf(sha256)', 'hkdf(sha384)', 'hkdf(sha512)', 'pbkdf2(sha256)', 'pbkdf2(sha1)'
  out_algo[64]:      algorithm the derived key will be used for (e.g. 'cbc(aes)'); determines KEY fd type
  out_keylen:        derived key length in bytes (max 64 for v1)
  ikm_fd:            KEY fd holding HKDF IKM; -1 = use data written via write()
  salt[64]:          salt bytes (HKDF: optional; PBKDF2: required)
  salt_len:          length of salt
  info[256]:         HKDF context/label (ignored for PBKDF2)
  info_len:          length of info
  iterations:        PBKDF2 iteration count (ignored for HKDF; framework enforces >= 1000)
  _pad[4]:           reserved

Fd lifecycle:
  - Caller opens an unset fd
  - For PBKDF2: write() the password (sensitive; framework stores temporarily, zeroizes after ioctl)
  - For HKDF with inline IKM: write() the IKM; OR set ikm_fd to a KEY fd
  - Call CRYPTO2DEV_IOC_DO_KDF
  - On success: fd is now a KEY fd holding the derived key; write() data is zeroized
  - read() on the KEY fd returns the public key if asymmetric, or is not applicable for symmetric

Provider callback:
  int (*kdf)(void *key_ctx,
             const char *algo,
             const u8 *ikm, u32 ikm_len,
             const u8 *salt, u32 salt_len,
             const u8 *info, u32 info_len,
             u32 iterations,
             u8 *out_key, u32 out_keylen);
  - Returns raw derived key bytes into out_key[]
  - Framework wraps out_key into a KEY fd via key_import internally, then memzero_explicit(out_key)
  - Provider never returns key bytes to userspace directly

Acceptance: DESIGN.md KDF section written and reviewed before implementation starts.
close_reason: DESIGN.md KDF section written: struct, fd lifecycle, provider callback, FIPS constraints
